mcqs.learning_point: Identify major parts of the human ear
mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT a major part of the human ear?
mcqs.explanation: The major parts of the human ear are the outer ear (pinna), the auditory canal, the middle ear ossicles, and the inner ear (cochlea, vestibule, semicircular canals). The larynx is part of the respiratory system, not the ear, so option D is incorrect and therefore the correct answer to the question.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand how vibrations reach the inner ear
mcqs.question: How do sound vibrations travel from the eardrum to the inner ear?

options.A: Through the auditory nerve directly to the brain
options.B: Via the ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) to the oval window of the cochlea
options.C: By passing through the eustachian tube into the inner ear
options.D: Through the semicircular canals which transmit vibrations

mcqs.answer: Via the ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) to the oval window of the cochlea
mcqs.explanation: When sound waves strike the eardrum, it vibrates. These vibrations are transmitted by the three middle‑ear bones – the malleus, incus and stapes – to the oval window, which then sets the fluid of the cochlea (inner ear) into motion. Options A, C and D describe incorrect pathways.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of the auditory nerve
mcqs.question: What is the primary function of the auditory (cochlear) nerve?

options.A: To amplify sound vibrations in the middle ear
options.B: To transmit electrical impulses from the cochlea to the brain for sound interpretation
options.C: To regulate pressure in the middle ear cavity
options.D: To protect the inner ear from loud noises

mcqs.answer: To transmit electrical impulses from the cochlea to the brain for sound interpretation
mcqs.explanation: The auditory nerve carries the neural signals generated by hair cells in the cochlea to the auditory cortex of the brain, where they are perceived as sound. It does not amplify sound (A), regulate pressure (C), or provide protection (D).

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the most effective method to protect your hearing while operating a loud electric drill?

options.B: Turning the drill to its lowest speed setting
options.C: Standing a few centimeters farther from the drill
options.D: Listening to music through headphones while drilling

mcqs.explanation: Earplugs or earmuffs attenuate the sound intensity reaching the ear, providing the greatest reduction in noise exposure. Reducing speed (B) may lower noise slightly but not enough; distance (C) helps only marginally; headphones (D) do not block external noise and can even increase risk.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify major parts of the human ear
mcqs.question: In the list below, which structure directly collects sound waves from the environment?
mcqs.explanation: The pinna is the external, funnel‑shaped part of the ear that captures sound waves and directs them into the auditory canal. The cochlea (B) is in the inner ear, the auditory nerve (C) transmits signals, and the semicircular canals (D) are involved in balance, not sound collection.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand how vibrations reach the inner ear
mcqs.question: A child has a blockage in the ear canal. How will this affect the transmission of sound vibrations to the inner ear?

options.A: It will have no effect because vibrations bypass the canal
options.B: It will reduce the amount of vibration reaching the eardrum, thereby decreasing transmission to the inner ear
options.C: It will increase the vibration intensity on the eardrum
options.D: It will cause vibrations to be transmitted directly to the auditory nerve

mcqs.answer: It will reduce the amount of vibration reaching the eardrum, thereby decreasing transmission to the inner ear
mcqs.explanation: The ear canal carries sound waves to the eardrum. A blockage dampens these waves, so the eardrum vibrates less, leading to weaker stimulation of the ossicles and reduced motion of the cochlear fluid. Options A, C, and D describe impossible or incorrect mechanisms.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise the role of the auditory nerve
mcqs.question: True or false: The auditory nerve amplifies sound before sending it to the brain.

options.C: Partially true – it amplifies low frequencies only
options.D: Partially true – it amplifies high frequencies only

mcqs.explanation: The auditory nerve does not amplify sound; it merely carries the electrical signals generated by the hair cells of the cochlea to the brain. Amplification occurs in the middle ear (ossicles), not in the nerve. Hence the statement is false, making option B correct.

mcqs.question: Why is it recommended to limit exposure to sounds above 85 dB for more than 8 hours per day?

options.A: Because it can cause temporary hearing loss that recovers quickly
options.B: Because prolonged exposure can cause permanent damage to the hair cells of the cochlea
options.C: Because it improves the sensitivity of the ear over time
options.D: Because it reduces the production of ear wax

mcqs.answer: Because prolonged exposure can cause permanent damage to the hair cells of the cochlea
mcqs.explanation: Sound levels above 85 dB can damage the delicate hair cells in the cochlea if exposure is prolonged, leading to irreversible hearing loss. Temporary loss (A) is not the main concern, and options C and D are unrelated to noise exposure effects.
